clue.text: Local left in charge of a community

parts.note: your local is the pub nearest your home
L is the standard abbreviation for left
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone has gone off and left the pub in charge of village life.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the pub you habitually drink in.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, the public means the people of a place taken together, which is what a community is.

clue.text: Inspector in corporate get-together following normal example

indicators.note: the meeting comes after the word for normal

parts.note: par is the normal or average level

indicators.note: the police officer sits inside the meeting

parts.note: a company's Annual General Meeting
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police inspector turns up at a company's annual meeting as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a typical model or pattern, so it means an example.

clue.text: Like a puzzle Greek character in training begins

indicators.note: the Greek letter goes in among the other letters
training puts something into a new shape, so the letters of begins are reworked

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person in training is starting out, a puzzle to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' looks like part of the story of a Greek athlete, but it is the signal to rearrange 'begins'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemusing means perplexing or bewildering, which is the effect a puzzle has on someone.

clue.text: Singing comedienne blowing top, one averse to work

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and blowing it means losing it

parts.note: Bette Midler, American singer and comic actress

explanation.surface: A singing comic loses her temper with a lazy colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' reads as losing one's temper; here it removes the first letter of MIDLER.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who avoids work, so is someone averse to work.

clue.text: Indication GP is not working after Sunday

indicators.note: tells us the shuffled letters come behind the abbreviation for the day

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday

indicators.note: the letters are set to work in a new order, as if put through their paces

parts.note: these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A sign that the family doctor is off duty because it is Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is anything that points the way or gives a clue, so it is an indication.

clue.text: Priceless item in Basel damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up and its letters come out in another order

parts.note: these eleven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A priceless museum piece has been damaged in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Inestimable means too great to be valued, which is what priceless means.

clue.text: Breeze and wet weather in much of Borneo sadly

indicators.note: the wet weather sits inside the scrambled letters
sadly here means badly, so the letters are jumbled
much of a word is most of it, so Borneo loses its last letter

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A wind and rain over most of Borneo, sad news for the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breeze' wants to be wind, beside the wet weather, but it means an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is something needing no thought, and a breeze is likewise a task that is very easy.

clue.text: Unintelligible work, one somewhat devoid of appeal

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a musical work
a means one

indicators.note: devoid of means lacking, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: quite means somewhat, as in quite good
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A critic finds a piece of work obscure and rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: QUITE loses IT to leave QUE. 'It' for sex appeal dates from the 1920s film star Clara Bow, the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque writing is hard to see through or make sense of, so it is unintelligible.

clue.text: Like some parties in classic holiday area

wordplay.note: the Med, short for the Mediterranean, the traditional sunshine holiday destination

explanation.surface: Party-goers enjoy their celebrations in a favourite holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as THE MED, the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: A themed party has a dress code or decor built around one subject, as some parties do.

clue.text: Discover gang fight in New York?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to find someone out
second meaning: American slang for a street fight between gangs

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is American slang, hence New York.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage has rumble meaning detect a deception, while US slang uses it for a brawl between gangs.

clue.text: Film was screened, hosted by one in club mostly

indicators.note: something hosted by another is inside it, so the screening word goes within the club word
most of the word, so member loses its last letter

parts.note: a member is one who belongs to a club
a film that ran was shown, so ran

explanation.surface: A movie was shown at a club, hosted by one of its members.
explanation.walkthrough: MEMBE is member cut short; RAN goes in before its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: A membrane is a thin skin or layer, and a film is likewise a thin coating or sheet.

clue.text: Record latest of poor shoddy diet in bad repute

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last
shoddy means badly made, so the letters of diet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A record of a poor, shoddy diet that leaves someone with a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: DISC + R + EDIT (diet rearranged).
explanation.definitionFit: Discredit is loss of reputation or esteem, a state of disgrace or dishonour.

clue.text: Overbearing police turned up on time with a round figure in case

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the following pieces
in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

indicators.note: the round figure is set inside the legal case

parts.note: a court case is a trial
the letter O is round, like a zero

explanation.surface: Detectives arrive on time with a stout suspect, ready for a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictatorial manner is domineering, like a dictator's, so it is overbearing.

clue.text: A hint about temperature that's keenly perceptive

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the hint wraps itself around the letter, going about it

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A hint about the temperature from someone sharply observant.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute observer has sharp senses or insight, the synonym used here.

clue.text: Information journalist found in change of name for actor

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the journalist is found inside the rearranged letters
a change of a word rearranges its letters

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, especially a low-grade one

explanation.surface: Information about a journalist who changed his name for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, short for general information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Hackman was an American film star, Oscar winner for The French Connection and Unforgiven.

clue.text: Antagonism? It's possibly settled in Scottish island

indicators.note: everything else goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney islands

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters of It's

parts.note: lit, as a bird lit on a branch, means settled

explanation.surface: Is there hostility? Perhaps it has been settled on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' reads as resolved, but here it is a bird alighting; Hoy is an island in Orkney, off the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility is unfriendliness or opposition, a near synonym of antagonism.

clue.text: Fellowship left out by a Northern church for instruction

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces stand alongside each other
left out tells us the abbreviation for left is omitted

parts.note: a guild is an association or fellowship
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church fellowship in the north is excluded and left seeking direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, abandoned; it is L, removed from GUILD.
explanation.definitionFit: Guidance is advice or direction given to someone, the same sense as instruction.

clue.text: Be quiet like a cow — or prone to trembling?

parts.note: sh! is a call for silence
a made-up adjective, having an udder like a cow

explanation.surface: Telling someone to hush like a cow, or perhaps just nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: UDDERY is a joke coinage; the question mark at the end owns up to that and to the rare word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuddery is an informal adjective for given to shudders or quivering, hence trembling.

clue.text: Mark retirement of former student beside unrefined resort

indicators.note: signals that the next piece is placed alongside the previous ones

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: an old boy is a former pupil of a school
rough means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: An old school pupil retires to a seaside town, rough around the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school. Scarborough is a seaside resort on the Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarborough is a traditional English holiday town on the North Sea coast, an example of a resort.

clue.text: Good scope for opening comment

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
an ambit is the extent or scope of something

explanation.surface: A speaker has plenty of room to start a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a chess opening, a gambit is a remark made to start a conversation or gain an advantage.

clue.text: Artist capturing female group on rise in religious festival

indicators.note: the artist's name takes the other letters captive inside it

parts.note: Salvador Dalí, the Spanish surrealist painter

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

explanation.surface: A painter is caught up among a women's club during a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, an example of a religious festival.

clue.text: Excuse current in French town

indicators.note: the electrical symbol sits inside the name of the town

parts.note: Albi is a town in south-west France
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone excuses the current state of affairs in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used more loosely as any excuse or justification.

clue.text: Writer with aim to appear in dictionary that's adaptable

indicators.note: the words are shown appearing inside the reference book

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
a pen is something you write with
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A writer hopes to get into the dictionary, which is always changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-ended has no fixed limit and can be changed as needed, so it is adaptable.

clue.text: Possibly remove from club old footballer lacking energy

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter goes missing

parts.note: Pelé, the Brazilian football great
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A club might throw out an ageing player who has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: PELE drops its final E. 'Possibly' shows that removing from a club is just one example of expelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone out, and throwing a member out of a club is one instance.

clue.text: I bet a fancy motor racing company's head is supremely happy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are made over

parts.note: F1 is Formula One motor racing, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: I bet the boss of a motor racing team is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: BEATI is 'I bet a' rearranged; F1, written FI, is Formula One, the top motor racing series; C heads 'company's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatific means blissful, showing or giving heavenly joy.

clue.text: Drunkard creates pong emptying bottles

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so the run of words keeps the answer within

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A drunk smells bad as he empties one bottle after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptying bottles' looks like a picture of drinking; 'bottles' is the verb, holding the answer in the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is slang for a heavy drinker, one who soaks up alcohol as a sponge soaks up water.

clue.text: Hear agricultural implement is picked up in wheeled transport

indicators.note: picked up, as by a microphone or a listener, signals going by sound

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case; a sickle is a curved blade for cutting crops

explanation.surface: A farm tool being heard and lifted onto a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY and SICKLE, spoken aloud, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricycle is a three-wheeled pedal vehicle, so it is transport on wheels.

clue.text: Liable to crash?

parts.note: surface reading: a vehicle or computer prone to collisions or failures; setter's reading: crash is slang for falling asleep, as in crash out on the sofa

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the slang sense of crash, to fall asleep exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drowsy is ready to drop off at any moment, so they are likely to crash out.
